1g.title: Quick component estimator
1g.intro: The installed cost, the weight and the installation man-hours of any process plant component, in seconds.

reports.title: One report format: your brand, your client
reports.intro: Every Kpex 1G session and every Kpex 2G estimate prints as an Excel workbook with your logo and your client's.

a.title: Process Plant Components
a.intro: Parametric cost models for every component of a process plant — equipment, piping, fire & gas, instruments, electrical and civil works. In Kpex 2G each piece of process equipment comes together with its inside-battery-limits installation, shown graphically, on its way into a full AACE estimate.

a1.title: Process Equipment & ISBL
a1.intro: Rotating and static equipment, heat transfer, material handling and miscellaneous process equipment — each one together with its inside-battery-limits installation: the piping, instruments, electrical and civil works around it, shown graphically.

a2.title: Piping
a2.intro: Pipes, valves, fittings, strainers, hangers and supports, steam specialties and the fabrication and assembly activities of a piping system.

a3.title: Fire & Gas
a3.intro: Active and passive fire protection: fire pumps and their accessories, fire protection piping, hydrants, detection systems, suppression systems and passive firefighting measures.

a4.title: Instruments
a4.intro: Relief and control valves, level, pressure, flow and temperature instruments, distributed control systems, control panels and instrument tubing.

a5.title: Electrical
a5.intro: Power distribution and control, motor control stations, lighting and signals, heat tracing, raceways and conduit, hazardous-area equipment, cables and busways.

a6.title: Civil Works
a6.intro: Site preparation and infrastructure, building construction and finishing, concrete, masonry and structural steel works.

b.title: Historical Project Cost Benchmarks
b.intro: Cost curves and KPI ranges built from documented projects, to test an early estimate against what similar projects really cost before committing to an estimate class.

b1.title: Benchmark Cost Curves
b1.intro: Capacity–cost curves of complete facilities and project types, fitted on documented projects and grouped in families.

b2.title: KPI Ranges Library
b2.intro: Key performance indicators of capital projects — cost ratios, unit costs and percentages — with their typical ranges by facility family.

b3.title: Offshore Oil & Gas Benchmarks
b3.intro: Benchmarks of offshore developments — platforms, subsea systems and floating units — with their cost breakdown structures.

b4.title: Railway Benchmarks
b4.intro: Cost benchmarks of railway projects — lines, high-speed rail, stations and systems — by length and type.

c.title: Facilities Cost Models
c.intro: Parametric cost models for complete facilities — industrial plants, infrastructure, buildings, renewable energy, nuclear and mining — sized by capacity, from early feasibility through Class 3 estimates.

c1.title: Industrial Process Plants
c1.intro: Oil & gas production onshore and offshore, LNG, refineries, power, water, chemicals, food, pharmaceuticals, paper, metals, textiles, steam and chilled water, manufacturing, solid waste and plant retrofits.

c2.title: Infrastructure Projects
c2.intro: Nine infrastructure types: highways, railways, tunnels, airport runways, high-voltage lines, substations, pipelines, aqueducts and dams, each one estimated from capital cost to operation and decommissioning.

c3.title: Building Projects
c3.intro: Twenty building types, from offices, schools and hospitals to hotels, warehouses, airport terminals and control buildings, each one estimated element by element and carried through its operation and demolition.

c4.title: Renewable Energy Facilities
c4.intro: Twelve technologies: solar PV, onshore and offshore wind, battery storage, CSP, green hydrogen, hydropower, geothermal, bioenergy, power-to-X, hybrid systems and large heat pumps, each one estimated from capital cost to operation and decommissioning.

c5.title: Nuclear Projects
c5.intro: Six nuclear designs: large PWR, BWR, small modular reactors, CANDU / PHWR, HTGR and Generation IV, and life extension of existing units — each one estimated from capital cost to operation and decommissioning.

c6.title: Mining Projects
c6.intro: Six mine types: open-pit copper, underground gold, open-pit coal, iron ore, copper heap leach and lithium — each one estimated from capital cost to operation and mine closure.

d.title: Operating Cost (OPEX)
d.intro: Operating cost of process plants: manufacturing cost per unit of product, split into raw materials, utilities, labour and depreciation, and scaled to the plant capacity.

d1.title: OPEX Cost Estimator
d1.intro: The operating cost of 80 plant types in nine sectors — chemicals, food, power, water, refining, metals, mining, pulp and paper, and renewables — per unit of product and per year, for the capacity you enter.

e.title: Decommissioning (ABEX)
e.intro: Abandonment and decommissioning cost of oil & gas, process, renewable, mining and nuclear facilities — the end-of-life cost that completes the life-cycle estimate.

e11.title: Oil & Gas Onshore
e11.intro: Decommissioning of onshore oil & gas fields: 32 activities in six scope groups — process equipment, electrical and instrumentation, pipelines and piping, metal structures, civil structures, and wells and subsurface remediation.

e12.title: Oil & Gas Offshore
e12.intro: Decommissioning of offshore installations: 30 activities in seven scope groups — well P&A, topsides, jackets and substructures, subsea infrastructure, pipelines and risers, the marine spread and onshore disposal, and site remediation.

e2.title: Process Plants
e2.intro: Decommissioning of refineries, petrochemical and chemical plants, pharmaceuticals, fertilisers and industrial water and waste: 35 activities in six scope groups, from equipment dismantling and hazardous-material decontamination to environmental remediation and closure.

e3.title: Renewable Energy
e3.intro: End-of-life of renewable and new-technology facilities: 31 activities in six scope groups — onshore and offshore wind, solar PV, hydrogen and power-to-X, battery storage, and the shared site works and disposal.

e4.title: Mining
e4.intro: Mine closure: 23 activities in six scope groups — tailings storage closure, open pit and underground, plant demolition, water management and acid mine drainage, site rehabilitation, and post-closure monitoring.

e5.title: Nuclear
e5.intro: Decommissioning of nuclear facilities: 20 activities in six scope groups — reactor and primary systems dismantling, radioactive waste, spent fuel, balance of plant, site remediation and licence termination, and deferred storage.

z.title: Cost Estimation Support Tools
z.intro: The tools that turn a cost into an estimate: engineering and home office, labour and crews, rental equipment, location factors for 197 countries, the Kpex Cost Index and the assessment tools.

z1.title: Engineering & Home Office
z1.intro: Four tools for the engineering behind a project: engineering and supervision man-hours from the direct labour cost, their spread across 31 disciplines, the home-office services ratio, and engineering hours equipment by equipment.

z2.title: Construction Labour & Crews
z2.intro: The construction resources behind a Class 3 and Class 2 estimate: 173 labour crafts, 242 equipment types, 560 crews built from them, and 22,005 construction activities with their crew and productivity.

z3.title: Rental Equipment
z3.intro: The hourly cost of construction equipment, fully burdened (ownership + operating), by family, type and model — ready for Class 3 and Class 2 estimates.

z4.title: Location Factor
z4.intro: The CAF Location Factor Index: how much a capital project costs in each country compared with the US Gulf Coast.

z5.title: Kpex Cost Index
z5.intro: Monthly cost index of plant equipment, construction labour, engineering and buildings — one method, applied region by region.

z6.title: Assessment Tools
z6.intro: Project Definition Rating Index (PDRI) and estimate accuracy assessment.
